# Gastdirigat

## Working unit

One engagement where Ruben is invited to conduct somebody else's orchestra or at
somebody else's opera house. He is a guest: the house owns the schedule, the
orchestra and the library, and he owns his contract, his travel and his own
preparation.

The working unit is the project as the notebook records it, usually gathered on
a `CL` page — `CL Aufgaben`, but also `CL Status & Termine`, `CL Konditionen`,
`CL Abrechnungsoptionen` and others; the notebooks name them differently.
A project without one may still be a full working unit;
what decides is whether the section records enough to work from. Where it
records almost nothing, say the project is too thin to classify and ask.

## Classifying a project into this category

From what the pages record. The marks of a Gastdirigat:

- A contract with a fee, and the contract deciding who pays for travel and
  accommodation.
- Correspondence with an Orchestermanager, a KBB, an Intendanz or a
  Notenbibliothek at a house that is not the Gärtnerplatztheater.
- German promoters requiring a Umsatzsteuer-Befreiungsbescheinigung, and
  contracts asking for Finanzamt, Steuer-ID and bank details.

Guest engagements carry no shared prefix in the notebook — they are named for
the city or the piece. Classify from the contract and the counterparty.

## Expected evidence

Konzert- or Vorstellungstermine, Probenbeginn and Probenplan, contract status
and what it still lacks, Gage and how it compares to what he is paid elsewhere,
who pays for travel and accommodation and who books them, Noten — what he has,
what the library owes him, what he must buy — the Strichfassung where it is an
opera, his own score preparation, and the house contacts.

## The contract carries the logistics

The contract is where travel, accommodation and reimbursement are decided, so
its open fields are operational and not merely administrative. Reimbursement
caps, original receipts, Mitwirkendenkarten and tax certificates are all
recorded facts with their own deadlines when the contract states them.

Several performances spread across months mean several journeys, each with its
own booking and possibly its own fee arrangement. Do not let one travel
arrangement stand for a run.

An agency may sit between Ruben and the house — sometimes for the contract only.
Record which conversation each party owns. Some houses contract him directly and
the page says so; that is a fact worth carrying, because it decides who is
chased when the contract goes quiet.

**One agreement may cover several projects.** A house engaging him for a season
may settle a single Cachet covering every title in it, each title kept in its
own section. Where a page states that its fee is part of an agreement spanning
other productions, the fee is not renegotiated per title, and a condition
settled for one title may already hold for the others — say which page recorded
it rather than repeating it as though each had been agreed separately.

## The house owns the schedule and the library

The Probenplan comes from the house and is often provisional. The Notenbibliothek
supplies scores he does not have, receives his finished Strichfassung to
distribute, and transfers the Dramaturgie's Strichfassung into the singers'
Klavierauszüge. The Orchestermanagement owns Besetzung and Orchesterprobenpläne.
"CL Projekt-Etappen Übersicht" holds the full list of house contacts and what each
one wants; read it there rather than guessing from a name.

Announcing which work is rehearsed in which Probe is required wherever there are
several works or several Probenblöcke.

## Format

**Oper.** Rehearsal structure: musikalische Proben with the pianist → szenische
Proben with the director → Orchesterproben (OA → OSP → Bühnenproben →
Bühnenorchesterproben) → Hauptproben (HP1/Klavierhauptprobe →
Orchesterhauptprobe/HP2) → Generalprobe.

For a Neuproduktion the Strichfassung is worked out with the director and goes
to the Notenbibliothek. For a Wiederaufnahme it is requested from the house.
"CL Projekt-Etappen Übersicht" records the lead time for requesting it and the date
it counts back from; read it there and say the derived date was worked out.

At a konzertante Oper the Orchesteraufstellung on the stage is checked in time.

For a Barockoper: Verzierungen go to the singers, and Appoggiaturen in the
Rezitative apply to Barock and Wiener Klassik. The lead time is on the reference
page. Where the Probenbeginn is not recorded, that task is undatable rather than
undated, and the missing date is itself the next thing to find out.

**Konzert.** Orchesterproben → Hauptprobe → Generalprobe, sometimes with an
Anspielprobe at a second venue. Where the plan is marked provisional, gaps and
awkward spacing in it are worth raising with the house while the contract is
still going back and forth.

**Mischform.** A programme combining forces or genres — a concert work with a
concertante opera, or a large vocal-instrumental work. Musical rehearsals with
the soloists and singers; orchestral rehearsals less differentiated; Hauptprobe;
Generalprobe. An oratorio or Passion belongs here: chorus, children's chorus,
several soloists, Klavier- and Chorproben, continuo and period-instrument
questions, but no Strichfassung and no szenische Proben. Casting a continuo or
obbligato player is a substantive musical decision here, not a staffing detail.

## Workflow

1. Verify the headline facts — Termine, Probenbeginn, Gage, contract status —
   and find contradictory dates. Probenbeginn and Konzert are usually weeks
   apart and both are anchors for rules on the reference page.
2. Check what the contract still lacks and what it commits him to.
3. Establish what the house is waiting on and what he is waiting on from the
   house, and keep those two apart.
4. When the musician asks for outreach, Registrar extracts the contact, Envoy
   drafts, and Auditor verifies before the result is shown.

## Checks

- Contract sent, contract signed, contract returned and contract
  countersigned are four facts. Where two pages disagree on where the contract
  stands, `policy:divergence` governs.
- Fee, travel reimbursement and accommodation are separate arrangements, and
  each performance in a run may be paid differently from the first.
- Noten: what he owns, what the library will send, and what he must buy himself
  are three states. A score requested is not a score received.
- A single performance without rehearsals is still a production: a Sitz- or
  Einrichtungsprobe may be owed, and a date for it that has not been sent is an
  open point rather than an absent rehearsal.
- Where the house names one Probenbeginn in correspondence and its own detailed
  plan begins on another date, both are recorded facts and neither retires the
  other. A proposal to change the plan is a third state again: report all of
  them and say which is outstanding.
- A cancelled player or singer is a live problem with a replacement attached to
  it, and it usually outranks everything else on the page.
- Never infer that an Intendanz, a Studienleitung or an Orchesterbüro replied
  because the page records what was sent to them.
- Travel research based on current timetables is not a booking, and a
  connection that cannot yet be booked is a plan rather than a fact.
- A section holding only repertoire research is a project in its programming
  phase. Report the missing organisational facts as an inventory.

## Not this playbook

Work at the Gärtnerplatztheater is `project-type:gpt` — no contract, no fee, no
travel is the tell. A Bach Consort Wien engagement is `project-type:bcw`, even
at a house he also guest-conducts at.
